title: A rule for everyone
subtitle: From every object to this object.
theorem: (forall x : T, P x) -> P a
lesson: A universal fact can be used at any in-scope object of its input type. Applying it to a gives P a, not P b.
story: The workshop is waking up. This press has a rule for every object. Try it on a: a rule for everyone also covers this one object.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Assume the rule
actions.feedback: Introduce the universal rule Hall.

nodes.hint: Introduce the universal rule Hall. (intro Hall.)

actions.label: Use the rule for a
actions.feedback: Specialize Hall at a and keep the result as Ha.

actions.label: Use the rule for b
actions.feedback: That is a valid use of the rule, but it proves P b. The goal asks about a. Undo to follow the guided route.

nodes.hint: Specialize Hall at a and keep the result as Ha. (pose proof (Hall a) as Ha.)
This move is legal, but this guided lesson follows a different route. Inspect the goal and undo.

actions.label: Use the whole rule
actions.feedback: The goal asks for evidence about a. The rule must first be applied to that object.

actions.label: Use evidence for a
actions.feedback: Ha proves P a exactly.

nodes.hint: Ha proves P a exactly. (exact Ha.)
A universal fact can be used at any in-scope object of its input type. Applying it to a gives P a, not P b.

title: Pack a certificate
subtitle: An object and its evidence.
theorem: P a -> exists x : T, P x
lesson: To prove that something has a property, choose a witness and then supply evidence about that same object.
story: We have evidence about a. Pack a and its matching evidence together. That is enough to promise that something has the property.

actions.label: Assume evidence for a
actions.feedback: Keep the given proof of P a as Ha.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Keep the given proof of P a as Ha. (intro Ha.)

actions.label: Choose witness a
actions.feedback: We have P a, so choose a as the witness.

actions.label: Choose witness b
actions.feedback: Choosing b is legal, but the evidence is about another object. Compare the remaining goal, then undo.

actions.label: Choose unseen
actions.feedback: That object is not in scope. Choose an available object of type T.

nodes.hint: We have P a, so choose a as the witness. (exists a.)
This move is legal, but this guided lesson follows a different route. Inspect the goal and undo.

actions.label: Pack its evidence
actions.feedback: The remaining goal is P a, exactly what Ha proves.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: The remaining goal is P a, exactly what Ha proves. (exact Ha.)
To prove that something has a property, choose a witness and then supply evidence about that same object.

title: Open a sealed package
subtitle: Keep track of what you discover.
theorem: (exists x : T, P x /\ Q x) -> exists x : T, P x
lesson: Unpacking an existential introduces a witness and evidence about it. The witness is discovered, not chosen by you.
story: A package contains an unknown object and two facts about it. Open it carefully, keep its identity, and repack only the fact we need.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Accept the package
actions.feedback: Assume the existential certificate.

nodes.hint: Assume the existential certificate. (intro Hpackage.)

actions.label: Discover its witness
actions.feedback: Unpack a fresh x and its certificate Hboth.

actions.label: Use x before opening
actions.feedback: The package's witness is not available until you unpack it.

nodes.hint: Unpack a fresh x and its certificate Hboth. (destruct Hpackage as [x Hboth].)

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Unpack both facts
actions.feedback: Hboth contains P x and Q x.

nodes.hint: Hboth contains P x and Q x. (destruct Hboth as [HP HQ].)

actions.label: Keep witness x
actions.feedback: Repackage the same x, since HP concerns x.

actions.label: Choose witness b
actions.feedback: Choosing b is legal, but the evidence is about another object. Compare the remaining goal, then undo.

nodes.hint: Repackage the same x, since HP concerns x. (exists x.)
This move is legal, but this guided lesson follows a different route. Inspect the goal and undo.

actions.label: Use the other property
actions.feedback: HQ proves Q x. The goal needs P x, even though the object is the same.

actions.label: Keep the first fact
actions.feedback: HP proves P x; HQ is about the other property.

nodes.hint: HP proves P x; HQ is about the other property. (exact HP.)
Unpacking an existential introduces a witness and evidence about it. The witness is discovered, not chosen by you.

title: Build a general rule
subtitle: Any input, not a favorite example.
theorem: (forall x : T, P x /\ Q x) -> forall x : T, P x
lesson: To establish a universal goal, introduce an arbitrary object. A proof for a particular a does not establish the claim for every x.
story: This engine must work for any input. Take an arbitrary object x, use the two-part certificate for x, and keep its first fact.

actions.label: Assume the general rule
actions.feedback: Hall supplies both properties for every input.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Hall supplies both properties for every input. (intro Hall.)

actions.label: Use just the example a
actions.feedback: A certificate for a particular a is not a rule for every x.

actions.label: Take an arbitrary x
actions.feedback: Introduce an arbitrary x of type T.

nodes.hint: Introduce an arbitrary x of type T. (intro x.)

actions.label: Use the rule for x
actions.feedback: Apply Hall to this arbitrary x.

actions.label: Use the rule for a
actions.feedback: This is valid evidence about a. Our current goal is about arbitrary x, so undo to follow the guided route.

nodes.hint: Apply Hall to this arbitrary x. (pose proof (Hall x) as Hboth.)
This move is legal, but this guided lesson follows a different route. Inspect the goal and undo.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Unpack x's certificate
actions.feedback: Extract both properties of x.

nodes.hint: Extract both properties of x. (destruct Hboth as [HP HQ].)

actions.label: Return the first fact
actions.feedback: HP establishes P x for the arbitrary input.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: HP establishes P x for the arbitrary input. (exact HP.)
To establish a universal goal, introduce an arbitrary object. A proof for a particular a does not establish the claim for every x.

title: Open the gate
subtitle: The same key holder all the way through.
theorem: (exists x : T, Key x) -> (forall x : T, Key x -> Opens x) -> exists z : T, Opens z
lesson: Unpack the key holder, use the opening rule for that same person, and package the resulting opening evidence.
story: Someone carries a key. Our rule says every key holder can open the gate. Find that same person's opening certificate and package it.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Accept a key holder
actions.feedback: Assume someone has a key.

nodes.hint: Assume someone has a key. (intro Hholder.)

actions.label: Accept the opening rule
actions.feedback: Assume the rule for every key holder.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Assume the rule for every key holder. (intro Hrule.)

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Discover the key holder
actions.feedback: Unpack x and the proof Hkey : Key x.

nodes.hint: Unpack x and the proof Hkey : Key x. (destruct Hholder as [x Hkey].)

actions.label: Use the rule for x
actions.feedback: Hopen is now Key x → Opens x.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Hopen is now Key x → Opens x. (pose proof (Hrule x) as Hopen.)

actions.label: Choose witness b
actions.feedback: Choosing b is legal, but the evidence is about another object. Compare the remaining goal, then undo.

actions.label: Name x as the opener
actions.feedback: Choose the person whose key we actually have.

nodes.hint: Choose the person whose key we actually have. (exists x.)
This move is legal, but this guided lesson follows a different route. Inspect the goal and undo.

actions.label: Use x's opening rule
actions.feedback: To establish Opens x, Hopen asks for Key x.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: To establish Opens x, Hopen asks for Key x. (apply Hopen.)

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Present x's key
actions.feedback: Hkey supplies the required evidence.

nodes.hint: Hkey supplies the required evidence. (exact Hkey.)
Unpack the key holder, use the opening rule for that same person, and package the resulting opening evidence.

title: Compare guarantees
subtitle: One for everyone, or one for each?
theorem: (exists y : U, forall x : T, R x y) -> forall x : T, exists z : U, R x z
lesson: One shared witness works for each input. The reverse does not follow: different inputs may require different witnesses.
story: One tool works for everyone. Can we issue each customer a suitable tool? Use the shared witness, then check why the reverse promise is different.

actions.label: Accept a shared tool
actions.feedback: Assume one witness works for every input.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Assume one witness works for every input. (intro Hshared.)

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Unpack the shared tool
actions.feedback: Discover y : U and Hall, its rule for every x.

nodes.hint: Discover y : U and Hall, its rule for every x. (destruct Hshared as [y Hall].)

actions.label: Take any customer x
actions.feedback: Introduce an arbitrary input of type T.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Introduce an arbitrary input of type T. (intro x.)

actions.label: Issue the input x
actions.feedback: The witness must have type U. Our input x has type T; these types are not interchangeable.

actions.label: Issue the shared tool y
actions.feedback: Choose the witness that already works for everyone.

nodes.hint: Choose the witness that already works for everyone. (exists y.)

actions.label: Check this customer's fit
actions.feedback: Hall x gives R x y.

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

nodes.hint: Hall x gives R x y. (pose proof (Hall x) as Hxy.)

actions.label: Use an unseen fact
actions.feedback: That fact is not in this context. Use evidence that is actually available.

actions.label: Supply the fit certificate
actions.feedback: The same y works for this arbitrary x.

nodes.hint: The same y works for this arbitrary x. (exact Hxy.)
One shared witness works for each input. The reverse does not follow: different inputs may require different witnesses.
